content:
The Jio Platforms IPO closed on October 23, 2026, with 7.65 times oversubscription and 1.08 crore applications. Allotment finalizes October 26 on KFin Technologies' portal. Listing is October 28 on BSE and NSE, with the grey market implying a price near Rs 1,370, about 22% above the Rs 1,119 issue price. If you got allotment, most investors are better off holding than selling on day one. This is general information, not financial advice.

Key Takeaways

  • The Jio IPO attracted 1.08 crore applications and finished 7.65 times oversubscribed, so most retail applicants won't get allotment.
  • Allotment finalizes October 26; check on KFin Technologies' portal using your PAN or application number.
  • A grey market premium of about Rs 250 points to a listing price around Rs 1,370, roughly 22% above the issue price of Rs 1,119.
  • Hold for at least 12 months if you can: the long-term Jio story outweighs a quick listing-day flip.
  • If you missed allotment, wait a few days after listing before buying; listing-day prices often cool off.

What Happens on October 26 if You Applied?

Head to KFin Technologies' portal on October 26 and enter your PAN to check allotment. If you got shares, they credit to your demat account on October 27 and list on BSE and NSE on October 28. If you didn't, your blocked funds unblock the same day. Allotment and listing dates are tentative; check exchange notices for any change.

The registrar is KFin Technologies. You can search by PAN, application number, or demat account number. Results are usually up by mid-morning.

Will You Actually Get Jio IPO Allotment?

Most retail investors won't, and the math is blunt about it. The issue was subscribed 7.65 times overall. With 1.08 crore applications competing for a fixed retail pool, SEBI's computerized lottery awards one lot per lucky applicant. Each lot is 12 shares at Rs 1,119, worth about Rs 13,428.

Rough odds for retail: somewhere between 1 in 5 and 1 in 9, depending on how heavily the retail category was subscribed. You'll know October 26.

Should You Hold Jio Shares or Sell on Listing Day?

If you get allotment, hold for at least a year unless you need the cash. The GMP implies a listing price near Rs 1,370, about 22% above Rs 1,119, but GMP isn't a guarantee. Analysts at Motilal Oswal expected a listing pop of 10 to 15%, not the full 22%. Selling on day one captures a quick gain; holding preserves the upside if Jio compounds steadily over two to three years.

FactorSell on Listing DayHold for 12+ Months
Estimated gain10 to 25% (GMP-based estimate)Depends on business execution
Main riskGMP rarely matches actual listing priceStock may dip after initial pop
Best forShort-term traders needing liquidityInvestors with a 1 to 2 year horizon
DownsideMisses upside if stock doubles laterCapital locked if the stock corrects
Bottom lineFine if you need the cashBetter choice for most applicants

GMP is an unofficial, unregulated signal. It can shift overnight. Treat it as a rough directional read. Selling your full allotment on day one because the GMP looked good is, definately, the most common way retail investors leave money on the table in marquee IPOs.

What Does Jio Platforms Actually Look Like as a Business?

Jio posted revenue of about Rs 1.47 lakh crore in FY26, up roughly 15%, with a net profit of Rs 30,049 crore. Its subscriber base stands at 533 million as of June 2026. It runs India's largest 5G network and earns across digital services, broadband, and enterprise. That's scale.

The catch is valuation. At the Rs 1,119 issue price, Jio trades at roughly 34 to 35 times earnings, close to Bharti Airtel's multiple. Airtel earns a higher ARPU, Rs 257 against Jio's Rs 214, and has a lower PEG ratio of 0.84 against Jio's 2.2. Airtel looks cheaper on growth-adjusted terms right now. That doesn't make Jio a bad stock. It means a lot of future growth is already priced in.

The IPO is a fresh issue with no offer-for-sale component. The Rs 30,213 crore raised goes toward reducing Reliance's debt and funding Jio's expansion. Once the listing-day excitement has occured and settled, watch how the stock trades in the first month before deciding to add more shares.

Should You Buy Jio Shares on Listing Day if You Missed Allotment?

Probably not on day one. Stocks that list with a big pop often dip in the days after, once the initial buzz fades. If you missed allotment and still want exposure, wait a week or so, watch how it trades, and buy at a calmer price. Chasing a listing high is how retail investors overpay for stocks that then sit flat for months.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I check my Jio IPO allotment status on October 26?

Go to KFin Technologies' portal, select the Jio Platforms IPO, and enter your PAN or application number. Results are usually available by mid-morning on allotment day, October 26.

What is the expected Jio Platforms listing price on October 28?

The grey market premium before listing was about Rs 250 above the issue price of Rs 1,119, pointing to a listing range of Rs 1,360 to Rs 1,380. Actual listing prices often differ from GMP. Treat it as a directional signal, not a guarantee of what you'll see on October 28.

What happens to my funds if I don't get Jio IPO allotment?

If you applied through UPI-linked ASBA, the blocked amount is unblocked on allotment day, usually October 26. Funds should be available within hours, though the timing depends on your bank's processing speed.

Is Jio Platforms a good long-term investment after listing?

Jio has solid fundamentals: 533 million subscribers, India's largest 5G network, and growing digital revenue. The concern is valuation; at 34 to 35 times earnings, the stock needs consistent growth to justify the price. Analysts who gave a subscribe rating mostly had a two- to three-year horizon in mind, not a one-week flip.

Should I sell Jio shares if the stock opens flat on listing day?

A flat opening on October 28 means the market isn't excited right now, not that the stock has no value. Hold unless you need the money. Many large IPO stocks trade sideways for months before the story plays out. A flat open is not a reason to sell.

The Short Version

You'll find out October 26 whether you got Jio IPO allotment. If you did, hold for 12 months unless you're a short-term trader; the GMP-implied listing pop is real but not guaranteed, and the Jio business story is stronger as a two-year hold than a one-day exit. If you didn't get allotment, wait out the listing excitement before buying on the open market. This is general information, not financial advice. Your situation is your own.
